definitions.explanation: The curved path of a celestial body or spacecraft around another object due to gravity.
The rails on which trains or trams run.
Figuratively, the expected or proper course of action or development.

examples.japanese: {地球|ちきゅう}は{太陽|たいよう}の{周|まわ}りを{軌道|きどう}に{沿|そ}って{回|まわ}っている。
examples.english: Earth revolves around the sun along its orbit.

examples.japanese: {人工衛星|じんこうえいせい}を{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}せることに{成功|せいこう}した。
examples.english: They succeeded in putting the artificial satellite into orbit.

examples.japanese: {路面電車|ろめんでんしゃ}の{軌道|きどう}が{道路|どうろ}の{真|ま}ん{中|なか}を{走|はし}っている。
examples.english: The tram tracks run down the middle of the road.

examples.japanese: プロジェクトはようやく{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}った。
examples.english: The project has finally gotten on track.

notes:
USAGE: {軌道|きどう} has both literal (astronomy/transportation) and figurative uses.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}る (to get into orbit; to get on track)
・{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}せる (to put into orbit; to set on the right track)
・{軌道|きどう}を{外|はず}れる (to go off orbit/track)
・{軌道|きどう}{修正|しゅうせい} (course correction)

SCIENTIFIC TERMS:
・{円軌道|えんきどう} - circular orbit
・{楕円軌道|だえんきどう} - elliptical orbit
・{静止軌道|せいしきどう} - geostationary orbit

IDIOMATIC EXPRESSION: {軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}る is frequently used figuratively to mean that a project, business, or effort has reached a stable, successful state.
